e: From ‛nduja in the Southern Calabrian dialect (either the Reggino or the Chjàna subdialect) of Sicilian, borrowed from Old French andoille, ultimately from Latin indūcō (“cover, overlay”). Doublet of andouille.
q: Boccalone, a company in Oakland, Calif., that makes artisanal cured meat, has started producing nduja.
2009 May 20, Florence Fabricant, “Spreading the Word About Nduja”, in New York Times:
Salumi platters, at $8 a selection, built from the best examples she can find, including a spicy, spreadable salami called nduja.
